proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\eta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta)\), and let \(P_\eta\) be the observed law whose multinomial vector is \(\eta\).  For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), define the unconditional treated-arm, control-arm, and stratum masses
\[
r_x(\eta)=\sum_{y\in\mathcal Y}\eta_{x1y},\qquad
c_x(\eta)=\sum_{y\in\mathcal Y}\eta_{x0y},\qquad
p_x(\eta)=r_x(\eta)+c_x(\eta).
\tag{61}
\]
The observed-cell condition in \(\mathrm{def{:}regular\mbox{-}interior\mbox{-}region}\) gives
\[
r_x(\eta)\geq K\delta,qquad
c_x(\eta)\geq K\delta,qquad
p_x(\eta)\geq2K\delta.
\tag{62}
\]
Set \(\kappa_\delta=K\delta\).  Since \(p_x(\eta)\leq1\), (62) implies, for every candidate law in the regular region,
\[
e_x(\eta)=\frac{r_x(\eta)}{p_x(\eta)}
\geq r_x(\eta)\geq\kappa_\delta,
\qquad
1-e_x(\eta)=\frac{c_x(\eta)}{p_x(\eta)}
\geq c_x(\eta)\geq\kappa_\delta.
\tag{63}
\]
In particular,
\[
e_x(\eta)\in[\kappa_\delta,1-\kappa_\delta]
\quad\text{uniformly over }\eta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta).
\tag{64}
\]
This is the cross-law overlap bound used below.  It is derived from the regular-region cell floor; \(\mathrm{ass{:}overlap}\), which supplies overlap for the target observed law, is not transferred to other profiled laws.

We first put all programs on a fixed cone.  For every response-type cell, write
\[
h_{xij}=\frac{a_{xij}}{e_x(\eta)},
\qquad
k_{xij}=\frac{b_{xij}}{1-e_x(\eta)}.
\tag{65}
\]
The divisions are valid by (64).  On a positive response-type cell,
\[
\frac{q_{xij}/(1-q_{xij})}{e_x(\eta)/(1-e_x(\eta))}
=\frac{h_{xij}}{k_{xij}}.
\tag{66}
\]
Thus, with the closed-cone convention at a zero cell, the odds restriction in \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\mbox{-}class}\) is equivalent to membership in the parameter-independent polyhedral cone
\[
\mathcal W_\Gamma
=\left\{(h,k):
h_{xij}\geq0,\ k_{xij}\geq0,\
\Gamma h_{xij}-k_{xij}\geq0,\
\Gamma k_{xij}-h_{xij}\geq0
\text{ for every }x,i,j\right\}.
\tag{67}
\]
Observational compatibility and consistency, as collected in \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\mbox{-}class}\), transform the observed-margin and ATE equations into
\[
\begin{aligned}
r_x(\eta)\sum_i h_{xij}&=\eta_{x1j},\\
c_x(\eta)\sum_j k_{xij}&=\eta_{x0i},\\
\sum_{x,i,j}(j-i)
\{r_x(\eta)h_{xij}+c_x(\eta)k_{xij}\}&=t.
\end{aligned}
\tag{68}
\]
Denote (68) by \(A_\eta w=b_\eta(t)\), where \(w=(h,k)\).  From \(\mathrm{def{:}assignment\mbox{-}cost}\),
\[
F_\eta(w)
=\sum_{x,i,j}
\frac{r_x(\eta)c_x(\eta)(h_{xij}-k_{xij})^2}
{r_x(\eta)h_{xij}+c_x(\eta)k_{xij}},
\tag{69}
\]
with the closed perspective value zero when \(h_{xij}=k_{xij}=0\).  Indeed,
\[
d_{xij}=e_x(\eta)\{1-e_x(\eta)\}(h_{xij}-k_{xij}),
\qquad
s_{xij}=e_x(\eta)h_{xij}+\{1-e_x(\eta)\}k_{xij},
\tag{70}
\]
and multiplying the corresponding summand by \(p_x(\eta)\) yields (69).  The exact SOCP representation in \(\mathrm{def{:}socp}\), the attained frontier in \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\), and the bijection (65) therefore give
\[
C_{P_\eta}(t)
=\min\{F_\eta(w):w\in\mathcal W_\Gamma, A_\eta w=b_\eta(t)\}.
\tag{71}
\]
Summing the first two groups of equations in (68) and using (62) shows that every feasible \(w\) satisfies
\[
\sum_{i,j}h_{xij}=1,qquad
\sum_{i,j}k_{xij}=1,qquad
0\leq h_{xij},k_{xij}\leq1.
\tag{72}
\]

We next obtain a uniform bound on attained dual multipliers.  If \(\Theta_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta)\) is empty, the deterministic assertion is vacuous.  Otherwise, take the cone in (67) in its affine hull after deleting redundant faces.  The strict feasible array in \(\mathrm{def{:}regular\mbox{-}interior\mbox{-}region}\) has at least the declared slack \(\delta\) in every nonredundant original response-mass and odds-face inequality.  The two odds-face slacks transform as
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{xij}-\ell_x(a_{xij}+b_{xij})
&=\frac{e_x(\eta)\{1-e_x(\eta)\}}
{e_x(\eta)+\Gamma\{1-e_x(\eta)\}}
(\Gamma h_{xij}-k_{xij}),\\
u_x(a_{xij}+b_{xij})-a_{xij}
&=\frac{e_x(\eta)\{1-e_x(\eta)\}}
{1-e_x(\eta)+\Gamma e_x(\eta)}
(\Gamma k_{xij}-h_{xij}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{73}
\]
By (64) and \(\Gamma\geq1\), each scalar factor in (73) lies in the explicit interval
\[
\left[\frac{\kappa_\delta^2}{\Gamma},\frac14\right].
\tag{74}
\]
Moreover \(a_{xij}=e_x(\eta)h_{xij}\) and \(b_{xij}=\{1-e_x(\eta)\}k_{xij}\), and both diagonal factors lie in \([\kappa_\delta,1-\kappa_\delta]\).  Hence the declared original slack yields a positive, computable lower bound on every normalized nonredundant face slack of (67).  Dividing by the largest Euclidean norm among the finitely many face normals gives a computable \(\gamma_\delta>0\) such that the transformed strict feasible point is at distance at least \(\gamma_\delta\) from the relative boundary of \(\mathcal W_\Gamma\).  This construction depends only on \(\delta,\Gamma,K\), and \(|\mathcal X|\), through the derived bound \(\kappa_\delta=K\delta\).

The equality operator in (68) has full row rank.  The treated- and control-margin rows have disjoint variable supports and nonzero coefficients, bounded below by \(\kappa_\delta\) by (62).  The ATE row is not in their span: for any fixed \(x\), the vector whose only nonzero coordinates are \(h_{x,0,0}=1\) and \(h_{x,1,0}=-1\) is orthogonal to every margin row but has inner product \(r_x(\eta)\geq\kappa_\delta\) with the ATE row.  Here \(K\geq2\) makes both indicated response types available.  On the compact set
\[
\Delta_\delta
=\left\{\eta:\eta_{xzy}\geq\delta,
\ \sum_{x,z,y}\eta_{xzy}=1\right\},
\tag{75}
\]
the entries of \(A_\eta\) are continuous.  Since full row rank holds at every point of \(\Delta_\delta\), continuity of the smallest singular value gives the computable constant
\[
\sigma_\delta
=\min_{\eta\in\Delta_\delta}\sigma_{\min}(A_\eta)>0.
\tag{76}
\]
Thus the right inverse
\[
R_\eta=A_\eta^{\mathsf T}(A_\eta A_\eta^{\mathsf T})^{-1}
\tag{77}
\]
satisfies \(\|R_\eta\|_{2\to2}\leq\sigma_\delta^{-1}\).  If \(\Gamma=1\), the odds restriction forces \(q_{xij}=e_x\) and identifies a single ATE; hence \(D_P\) is a singleton and no nonempty \(\mathcal T_0\subset\operatorname{int}D_P\) exists.  The theorem is then vacuous.  We henceforth consider the nonvacuous case.

For \(y=(\alpha,\beta,\lambda)\), use the Lagrangian
\[
\mathcal L_\eta(w;y)
=F_\eta(w)+y^{\mathsf T}\{b_\eta(t)-A_\eta w\}.
\tag{78}
\]
Cellwise minimization of (78) on \(\mathcal W_\Gamma\) is precisely the constraint in \(\mathrm{def{:}dual}\).  Indeed,
\[
r_xh_{xij}+c_xk_{xij}=p_xs_{xij},
\qquad
r_xh_{xij}=p_xs_{xij}q_{xij},
\tag{79}
\]
so the coefficient on a cell ray is
\[
p_xs_{xij}\left\{
\frac{(q_{xij}-e_x)^2}{e_x(1-e_x)}
-q_{xij}\alpha_{xj}-(1-q_{xij})\beta_{xi}
-\lambda(j-i)\right\}.
\tag{80}
\]
Therefore \(\mathrm{thm{:}explicit\mbox{-}dual}\) supplies an attained multiplier \(y_\eta(t)\) with
\[
C_{P_\eta}(t)
=\inf_{w\in\mathcal W_\Gamma}
\mathcal L_\eta(w;y_\eta(t)).
\tag{81}
\]

Let \(w^\circ\) be the uniformly strict feasible point, put
\(
\tau_\delta=\gamma_\delta\sigma_\delta/2
\), and let \(z\) be a unit vector in the equality space.  Equations (76)--(77) imply
\[
w^\pm=w^\circ\pm\tau_\delta R_\eta z\in\mathcal W_\Gamma,
\qquad
A_\eta w^\pm=b_\eta(t)\pm\tau_\delta z.
\tag{82}
\]
The vectors \(w^\pm\) range over a compact set: (72) bounds \(w^\circ\), while the perturbation has Euclidean norm at most \(\gamma_\delta/2\).  For \(r,c\geq\kappa_\delta\) and \(h,k\geq0\),
\[
0\leq\frac{rc(h-k)^2}{rh+ck}
\leq\frac{(h+k)^2}{\kappa_\delta(h+k)}
=\frac{h+k}{\kappa_\delta},
\tag{83}
\]
where the zero case uses the closed perspective convention.  Thus (69), (82), and (83) give a computable uniform \(\overline F_\delta<\infty\) such that \(F_\eta(w^\pm)\leq\overline F_\delta\).  Evaluating (81) at \(w^+\) and \(w^-\), respectively, and using \(C_{P_\eta}(t)\geq0\), yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_\delta y_\eta(t)^{\mathsf T}z
&\leq F_\eta(w^+)-C_{P_\eta}(t)\leq\overline F_\delta,\\
-\tau_\delta y_\eta(t)^{\mathsf T}z
&\leq F_\eta(w^-)-C_{P_\eta}(t)\leq\overline F_\delta.
\end{aligned}
\tag{84}
\]
Taking the supremum over unit \(z\), and converting Euclidean to \(\ell_1\) norm in the \(d=2|\mathcal X|K+1\) dimensional equality space, gives
\[
\|y_\eta(t)\|_1
\leq B_\delta
:=\frac{\sqrt d\,\overline F_\delta}{\tau_\delta}<\infty
\tag{85}
\]
uniformly over \(\eta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta)\) and \(t\in\mathcal T_0\).  Equations (63), (73)--(77), and (83)--(85) are an explicit finite-dimensional recipe for \(B_\delta\); no active-set stability is used.

We now compare two observed laws without transporting a dual certificate.  Let \(\eta,\eta'\in\Theta_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta)\), fix \(t\in\mathcal T_0\), put \(d_\infty=\|\eta-\eta'\|_\infty\), and let \(w'\) be a primal optimizer of (71) for \((\eta',t)\).  Define
\[
\psi_{r,c}(h,k)=\frac{rc(h-k)^2}{rh+ck}.
\]
On \(r,c\geq\kappa_\delta\), direct differentiation, \(|h-k|\leq h+k\), and \(rh+ck\geq\kappa_\delta(h+k)\) give
\[
|\partial_r\psi_{r,c}(h,k)|
\leq\frac{h+k}{\kappa_\delta}+\frac{h}{\kappa_\delta^2},
\qquad
|\partial_c\psi_{r,c}(h,k)|
\leq\frac{h+k}{\kappa_\delta}+\frac{k}{\kappa_\delta^2}.
\tag{86}
\]
At \(h=k=0\), the function is identically zero in \((r,c)\), so the same bounds hold.  Each arm mass changes by at most \(Kd_\infty\).  Summing (86) and using (72) therefore yields
\[
|F_\eta(w')-F_{\eta'}(w')|
\leq K_Fd_\infty,
\qquad
K_F=2|\mathcal X|K
\left(\frac{2}{\kappa_\delta}+\frac{1}{\kappa_\delta^2}\right).
\tag{87}
\]
Likewise, direct use of (68) and (72) gives
\[
\left\|
\{b_\eta(t)-A_\eta w'\}
-\{b_{\eta'}(t)-A_{\eta'}w'\}
\right\|_\infty
\leq K_A d_\infty,
\tag{88}
\]
where one may take
\[
K_A=\max\{1+K,\,2|\mathcal X|K(K-1)\}.
\tag{89}
\]
For a margin row, the bound in (88) is \(d_\infty+Kd_\infty\).  For the ATE row, it is at most \((K-1)\sum_x\{|r_x-r_x'|+|c_x-c_x'|\}\), proving (88)--(89).

Use the attained dual \(y_\eta(t)\) only in its own saddle identity (81), and evaluate that identity at \(w'\).  Since \(w'\in\mathcal W_\Gamma\), \(b_{\eta'}(t)-A_{\eta'}w'=0\), and \(F_{\eta'}(w')=C_{P_{\eta'}}(t)\), equations (81), (85), (87), and (88) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
C_{P_\eta}(t)
&\leq\mathcal L_\eta(w';y_\eta(t))\\
&=C_{P_{\eta'}}(t)
+F_\eta(w')-F_{\eta'}(w')
+y_\eta(t)^{\mathsf T}\{b_\eta(t)-A_\eta w'\}\\
&\leq C_{P_{\eta'}}(t)
+(K_F+B_\delta K_A)d_\infty.
\end{aligned}
\tag{90}
\]
Interchanging \(\eta\) and \(\eta'\) proves
\[
|C_{P_\eta}(t)-C_{P_{\eta'}}(t)|
\leq(K_F+B_\delta K_A)\|\eta-\eta'\|_\infty.
\tag{91}
\]
This is a cross-parameter saddle comparison on the common cone (67); no multiplier for one law is claimed feasible for the other law.  By \(\mathrm{def{:}regular\mbox{-}profile\mbox{-}band}\),
\[
L_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta)
\leq K_F+B_\delta K_A<\infty.
\tag{92}
\]
For example,
\[
\mathfrak B_\delta=(1+K_F+K_A)(1+B_\delta)
\tag{93}
\]
is a computable uniform \(\ell_1\)-bound for the attained cellwise dual multipliers and also bounds the modulus in (92).  This proves the deterministic and computability assertions.

It remains to prove the simultaneous finite-sample statement.  Fix a multinomial coordinate, let \(U\) be its cell indicator, and put \(p=E_PU\).  For
\[
g(\lambda)=\log E_P\exp\{\lambda(U-p)\},
\]
we have \(g(0)=g'(0)=0\), while \(g''(\lambda)\) is the variance of a Bernoulli variable under exponential tilting and is at most \(1/4\).  Integrating twice gives
\[
E_P\exp\{\lambda(U-p)\}\leq\exp(\lambda^2/8).
\tag{94}
\]
Independence in \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid\mbox{-}sampling}\), Markov's inequality, and optimization at \(\lambda=4r_n\) then give
\[
P\{|\widehat\theta_k-\theta_k|>r_n\}
\leq2\exp(-2nr_n^2)=\frac{\alpha}{M}.
\tag{95}
\]
A union bound over the \(M\) cells proves
\[
P\{\|\widehat\theta-\theta\|_\infty\leq r_n\}
\geq1-\alpha.
\tag{96}
\]
On the event in (96), the maintained membership \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta)\) implies \(\theta\in\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\).  The definitions of the two envelopes therefore give, simultaneously for every \(t\in\mathcal T_0\),
\[
\underline C_n(t)\leq C_P(t)\leq\overline C_n(t).
\tag{97}
\]
Any two multinomial vectors in \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\) are at \(\ell_\infty\)-distance at most \(2r_n\).  Applying the definition of \(L_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta)\), and then taking the supremum and infimum over this same nonempty set, gives on (96), again simultaneously in \(t\),
\[
0\leq\overline C_n(t)-\underline C_n(t)
\leq2L_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta)r_n.
\tag{98}
\]
Equations (92), (96), (97), and (98) establish every assertion of the theorem.

proposed.comparator_claim: The average-case sensitivity model leads to sharp bounds for \(E[Y(0)]\) and \(E[Y(1)]\), respectively.
The estimated range converges to the narrowest possible interval that must contain the true treatment effect.
Equations (10), (12), and (14) motivate the note-defined box-augmented Neyman specialization; the note proves only a one-way cost-nonincreasing map from compatible full laws into that specialization.
Monotone treatment response is maintained as a substantive restriction on individual response behavior.
The paper derives a Hadamard directional derivative for finite-valued Slater-regular linear SOCP optimal values.
An alternative resampling scheme is proposed which remains consistent when the bootstrap fails.
The paper develops uniform derivative-bootstrap inference for finite-valued function-valued optimization maps.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The Ishikawa--He--Kanamori comparison is a one-way cost-nonincreasing map into the note-defined box-augmented Neyman specialization of equation (14), not a strict tightening of the unqualified published class.

prose_updates.tldr: A finite observed law is lifted to one joint law of treatment and both potential outcomes, and the least Pearson assignment information needed to support each ATE is profiled. The attained sharp frontier has a perspective SOCP and explicit dual. For binary outcomes, a treatment-independent garbling removes the minority discordant response type without imposing monotone treatment response and without increasing any convex assignment cost; this yields the complete six-face scalar catalog and a squared-correlation null identity. A one-way, cost-nonincreasing embedding into the note-defined box-augmented Neyman specialization of Ishikawa--He--Kanamori equation~(14) gives the exact separation \(9/70>9/91\). With neighborhood radius at most \(1/10\), explicit positive mass, support, arm-variance, and treatment-variance bounds make continuity preserve a uniformly positive gap on a positive-volume open neighborhood. On the named uniformly Slater-regular multinomial region, the observed-cell floor itself gives \(e_x\) and \(1-e_x\) at least \(K\delta\) for every profiled law; a fixed-odds-cone parametrization, uniform equality right inverse, and bounded attained cellwise dual multipliers then yield a finite-sample \(O(n^{-1/2})\) profile diameter without transporting a dual certificate between laws. A contiguous boundary pair shows that honest bands must retain infinite diameter at a finite-to-infinite null-cost boundary.

project_justification.gap: Average-case sensitivity analysis has sharp armwise potential-outcome bounds but no jointly attained ATE frontier. Ishikawa--He--Kanamori's equations~(10), (12), and (14) provide an observed-policy-first divergence and Jensen--CMC computation, but they do not establish that their armwise weights are generated by one cross-world-compatible assignment law. The present comparison therefore requires a one-way full-law embedding into a separately defined box-augmented Neyman specialization on the same budget scale; it neither identifies nor strictly tightens the unqualified published class. Existing inference theory also does not quantify both the regular finite-sample width and the finite-to-infinite boundary obstruction for this frontier.
project_justification.niche: Finite outcomes make the missing joint law explicit, expose a response-type garbling geometry invisible to armwise reweighting, and permit an interior finite-dimensional comparison. Explicit neighborhood bounds show that the rational comparison is robust on a positive-volume set rather than a knife-edge witness.
project_justification.fill: The project profiles the exact full-law Pearson cost, certifies it by primal and dual conic programs, solves the binary geometry, and maps every compatible full law one way into the note-defined box-augmented Neyman specialization of Ishikawa--He--Kanamori equation~(14) at no greater cost. It proves the exact values \(9/70\) and \(9/91\), then uses a radius no larger than \(1/10\), strictly interior scalar optimizers, and explicit positive support and variance bounds to obtain a uniform positive gap on a nonempty open neighborhood. It also pairs a finite-sample regular-region diameter theorem, whose cross-law overlap is derived directly from the observed-cell floor, with a contiguous boundary lower bound.

prose_updates.related_work: Zhang and Zhao motivate average rather than worst-case assignment distortion and prove sharp bounds for each average potential outcome, but their discussion explicitly withholds joint ATE attainment. Ishikawa, He, and Kanamori define an observed-policy-first \(f\)-divergence in equation~(10), apply Jensen in equation~(12), and combine the relaxed divergence with CMC in equation~(14). The comparison here is deliberately one way: every compatible full law induces a feasible point of the note-defined box-augmented Neyman specialization with no larger cost. No equality with, strict tightening of, or reverse realizability for their unqualified published class is claimed. The rational witness has values \(9/70\) and \(9/91\); after restricting the coordinate radius to at most \(1/10\), explicit positive lower bounds for neighborhood mass, observable support, arm variance, and treatment variance make the strictly positive gap uniform on a positive-volume open neighborhood. Balke and Pearl supply the finite response-type representation, and Manski supplies the substantive monotone-response benchmark; the binary garbling result instead derives monotone support for an extremal compatible law without assuming monotone treatment response of the population. The regular finite-sample theorem rescales response-type masses onto a common odds cone. For every profiled law, its observed-cell floor yields \(e_x\geq K\delta\) and \(1-e_x\geq K\delta\); the proof then derives a uniform right inverse and multiplier bound and compares laws through each law's own saddle identity. Duan, Zhang, and Zhang derive directional derivatives for finite-valued Slater-regular SOCP values, while Fang and Santos and Firpo, Galvao, and Parker supply derivative-aware statistical inference; extending those tools through zero perspective cells and moving faces remains the open tangent-inference question.
prose_updates.interpretation: For computation across a finite covariate alphabet, additivity of the ATE and Pearson cost permits the observation \(C_P(t)=\min\{\sum_x p_x C_x(t_x):\sum_xp_xt_x=t\}\), with conditional minimizers glued stratum by stratum into a compatible full law. This is used as a computational decomposition, not retained as a numbered proposition. Substantively, the frontier reports the least assignment information required by a jointly compatible potential-outcome law; the note-defined Jensen--CMC value is a one-way lower-cost screen and not a certificate of reverse cross-world realizability.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The interior binary stationarity equation is generically quintic, so the exact catalog isolates a unique algebraic root and does not promise universal radical formulas. The regular-profile constant depends on the fixed-cone interior radius and the smallest singular value of the equality operator. Its cross-law coefficient bounds use the explicit regular-region overlap \(\kappa_\delta=K\delta\), derived from the observed-cell floor, and can deteriorate as \(\delta\) approaches zero. The boundary lower bound shows that this deterioration reflects a genuine statistical discontinuity at the null-feasibility boundary.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The sharpness, dual attainment, garbling, scalar catalog, one-way cost transfer into the note-defined box-augmented Neyman specialization, exact rational separation, positive-volume open-neighborhood uniform gap, regular-region finite-sample diameter, and boundary impossibility are theorem claims proved in the note. The comparison does not identify that specialization with Ishikawa--He--Kanamori's unqualified published class, does not claim a strict tightening of that class, and does not assert that every relaxed armwise weight is induced by a compatible cross-world assignment law. The local comparison uses radius at most \(1/10\) and records explicit positive lower bounds for neighborhood mass and observable support, arm variance, and treatment variance. The regular diameter proof derives cross-law overlap from the regular-region cell floor and controls coefficient movement through a common fixed odds cone and a law-specific saddle comparison; it does not claim active-set stability or feasibility of one law's dual certificate at another law. The finite-stratum infimal-convolution identity is retained only as a computational observation. Uniform tangent inference through zero perspective cells, optimizer ties, and moving odds faces remains open. The \(\Gamma=1\) specialization is retained only as a regression corollary. The application target remains a prespecified categorical mercury score and finite covariate stratification; it does not claim to recover the original continuous-outcome NHANES estimand.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem converts multinomial concentration into an honest finite-sample simultaneous band with \(O(n^{-1/2})\) diameter. For every profiled law in the named regular region, summing the positive cells in each treatment arm gives the explicit cross-law bounds \(e_x\geq K\delta\) and \(1-e_x\geq K\delta\); these bounds support the common-cone scaling, coefficient estimates, equality right inverse, and attained-multiplier bound.
statement_notes.gap: ZhangZhao2026AverageCase gives regular bands for armwise sensitivity curves; it does not control the finite-sample diameter of a jointly compatible ATE cost frontier through an observed-cell-derived cross-law overlap bound, a uniform fixed-cone Slater radius, and a law-specific saddle comparison.
statement_notes.consumer: The categorical-mercury analysis obtains a finite-width simultaneous frontier band whenever its prespecified cells and ATE range satisfy the reported observed-cell, cone-slack, and equality-rank margins; it need not assume that the true-law overlap constant automatically applies to every profiled multinomial law.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix one stratum and suppress its \(x\)-subscript.  The standing overlap condition gives \(0<e_x<1\).  Let \(Q\in\mathcal H_\Gamma(P)\), put
\[
s_{ij}=Q\{Y(0)=i,Y(1)=j\},
\qquad
q_{ij}=Q\{Z=1\mid Y(0)=i,Y(1)=j\}
\]
on every positive-mass response type, and use arbitrary versions on zero-mass types.  The odds restriction in \(\mathcal H_\Gamma(P)\) gives
\[
0<\ell_x\leq q_{ij}\leq u_x<1
\tag{1}
\]
whenever \(s_{ij}>0\).  Consistency and observational compatibility identify \(Y\) with \(Y(1)\) in the treated arm and with \(Y(0)\) in the control arm.

Choose versions of the conditional expectations defining \(w_Q\) that lie in the declared boxes on null observed cells.  On positive observed cells, iterated finite summation and the definition of \(w_Q\) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
e_xE_P\{w_Q(Y,1)\mid Z=1\}
&=E_Q\{Z w_Q(Y(1),1)\}\\
&=E_Q\!\left\{\frac{Z}{q_{Y(0),Y(1)}}\right\}
=\sum_{i,j:s_{ij}>0}s_{ij}q_{ij}\frac1{q_{ij}}=1,
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
and, identically,
\[
(1-e_x)E_P\{w_Q(Y,0)\mid Z=0\}
=E_Q\!\left\{\frac{1-Z}{1-q_{Y(0),Y(1)}}\right\}=1.
\tag{3}
\]
By (1), conditional averaging preserves the relevant intervals, so
\[
e_xw_Q(y,1)\in[e_x/u_x,e_x/\ell_x],
\qquad
(1-e_x)w_Q(y,0)
\in[(1-e_x)/(1-\ell_x),(1-e_x)/(1-u_x)].
\tag{4}
\]
Equations (2)--(4) are precisely the normalization and box restrictions in the note-defined, box-augmented Neyman specialization \(\mathcal W^{\mathrm{IHK}}_\Gamma(P)\) of Ishikawa--He--Kanamori equation~(14).  Hence
\[
w_Q\in\mathcal W^{\mathrm{IHK}}_\Gamma(P).
\tag{5}
\]
This establishes only a map from the compatible full-law class into that specialization; no converse realizability assertion is used or claimed.

The same cancellation proves preservation of the causal target:
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P\{Zw_Q(Y,1)Y\}
&=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}q_{ij}\frac{j}{q_{ij}}
=E_Q\{Y(1)\},\\
E_P\{(1-Z)w_Q(Y,0)Y\}
&=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}(1-q_{ij})\frac{i}{1-q_{ij}}
=E_Q\{Y(0)\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
Thus a full law in the ATE fiber \(T(Q)=\tau\) maps to a weight in the same ATE slice of the box-augmented program.

We next compare the costs.  Since \(a_{ij}=s_{ij}q_{ij}\) and \(b_{ij}=s_{ij}(1-q_{ij})\),
\[
d_{ij}=(1-e_x)a_{ij}-e_xb_{ij}=s_{ij}(q_{ij}-e_x).
\tag{7}
\]
The closed-perspective definition of \(R_P\) therefore gives
\[
R_P(Q)=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}\frac{(q_{ij}-e_x)^2}{e_x(1-e_x)},
\tag{8}
\]
where a zero-mass type contributes zero.  For the observed-policy-first orientation and \(f_N(r)=r^{-1}-1\), direct algebra on each positive-mass type gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&q_{ij}f_N(e_x/q_{ij})
+(1-q_{ij})f_N((1-e_x)/(1-q_{ij}))\\
&\qquad=\frac{q_{ij}^2}{e_x}
+\frac{(1-q_{ij})^2}{1-e_x}-1
=\frac{(q_{ij}-e_x)^2}{e_x(1-e_x)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
Consequently, the unrelaxed latent-law divergence in this orientation is exactly (8).

It remains to show that observed-cell averaging cannot increase this cost.  For a finite probability vector \((\lambda_k)_k\), positive numbers \((r_k)_k\), and \(S=\sum_k\lambda_kr_k\), symmetrization gives the elementary identity
\[
\sum_k\lambda_k f_N(r_k)-f_N(S)
=\frac{1}{S}\sum_{k<l}
\lambda_k\lambda_l\frac{(r_k-r_l)^2}{r_kr_l}\geq0.
\tag{10}
\]
Indeed, multiplying the left side by \(S\) and pairing the \((k,l)\) and \((l,k)\) summands gives exactly the numerator on the right.  Apply (10) within each positive observed \((Y,Z)\) cell, with \(r=e_x/q_{ij}\) in the treated arm and \(r=(1-e_x)/(1-q_{ij})\) in the control arm.  By the definition of \(w_Q\), the corresponding cell averages are \(e_xw_Q(y,1)\) and \((1-e_x)w_Q(y,0)\).  Summing the resulting inequalities over observed cells and using (8)--(9) proves
\[
\mathscr R_{\mathrm{IHK},P}(w_Q)\leq R_P(Q).
\tag{11}
\]
Thus (5), (6), and (11) are a one-way, cost-nonincreasing embedding into the note-defined box-augmented specialization.  Taking the infimum over compatible full laws on the ATE slice gives
\[
\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_P(\tau)\leq C_P(\tau).
\tag{12}
\]

For the budget equivalence in the relaxed program, delete coordinates corresponding to null observed cells.  Every remaining normalized weight coordinate lies in a closed, bounded interval whose lower endpoint is strictly positive by overlap and (4).  The normalization and ATE restrictions are closed affine constraints.  Hence a nonempty ATE slice is compact.  The objective is continuous on it because \(f_N\) is continuous on the positive box, so its infimum is attained.  It follows that the relaxed slice contains a weight of cost at most \(\rho\) if and only if \(\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_P(\tau)\leq\rho\).  The corresponding full-law attainment and budget equivalence are supplied by \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\); (5)--(12) give the asserted same-budget one-way implication.

Now set \(e_x=1/2\), \(p_1=4/5\), \(p_0=1/5\), \(\Gamma=4\), and \(\tau=3/10\).  For a feasible weight put
\[
r_1(y)=e_xw(y,1),\qquad r_0(y)=(1-e_x)w(y,0),
\]
and let \(m_z\) be the mean of \(Y\) under the normalized reweighting in arm \(z\).  Binary support and armwise normalization imply, and are implied by,
\[
r_1(1)=\frac{m_1}{p_1},\quad
r_1(0)=\frac{1-m_1}{1-p_1},\qquad
r_0(1)=\frac{m_0}{p_0},\quad
r_0(0)=\frac{1-m_0}{1-p_0}.
\tag{13}
\]
For any \(p,m\in(0,1)\), substitution into the armwise Neyman objective gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
p f_N(m/p)+(1-p)f_N((1-m)/(1-p))
&=\frac{p^2}{m}+\frac{(1-p)^2}{1-m}-1\\
&=\frac{(m-p)^2}{m(1-m)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
Because the two treatment probabilities are \(1/2\), (14) makes the total objective exactly
\[
J(m_1,m_0)
=\frac12\frac{(m_1-4/5)^2}{m_1(1-m_1)}
+\frac12\frac{(m_0-1/5)^2}{m_0(1-m_0)}.
\tag{15}
\]
The weighted ATE restriction is \(m_1-m_0=3/10\).

Here \(\ell_x=1/5\) and \(u_x=4/5\), so both boxes for \(r_z(y)\) are \([5/8,5/2]\).  Imposing that box on both coordinates in (13) is equivalent to
\[
m_1\in[1/2,7/8],\qquad m_0\in[1/8,1/2].
\tag{16}
\]
Writing \(m_0=x\) and \(m_1=x+3/10\), the exact feasible slice in (16) is \(x\in[1/5,1/2]\).

For \(g_p(m)=(m-p)^2/\{m(1-m)\}\),
\[
g_p''(m)=\frac{2p^2}{m^3}+\frac{2(1-p)^2}{(1-m)^3}>0.
\tag{17}
\]
Thus the sliced objective is strictly convex.  The identity \(g_{4/5}(m)=g_{1/5}(1-m)\) makes its derivative vanish at
\[
(m_1,m_0)=(13/20,7/20),
\tag{18}
\]
which is in the relative interior of (16), and hence is the unique minimizer.  Evaluation gives
\[
\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_P(3/10)
=J(13/20,7/20)
=\frac{(3/20)^2}{(13/20)(7/20)}
=\frac9{91}.
\tag{19}
\]
By the already established \(\mathrm{thm{:}symmetric\mbox{-}family}\), the same observed law and odds cap satisfy
\[
C_P(3/10)
=\frac{(3/5-3/10)^2}{1-3/10}
=\frac9{70}.
\tag{20}
\]
Therefore
\[
C_P(3/10)-\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_P(3/10)
=\frac9{70}-\frac9{91}
=\frac{27}{910}>0.
\tag{21}
\]
This proves the exact strict separation while maintaining only the one-way comparison with the explicitly defined box-augmented specialization.

Parameterize a one-stratum binary observed law by
\[
\theta=(e,p_1,p_0)\in(0,1)^3,
\]
where \(e=e_x\).  The four observable probabilities for \((Z,Y)=(1,1),(1,0),(0,1),(0,0)\) are
\[
ep_1,\qquad e(1-p_1),\qquad(1-e)p_0,\qquad(1-e)(1-p_0).
\tag{22}
\]
On the positive-cell region the inverse map is
\[
e=P(Z=1),\qquad
p_1=\frac{P(Z=1,Y=1)}{P(Z=1)},\qquad
p_0=\frac{P(Z=0,Y=1)}{P(Z=0)},
\tag{23}
\]
so this is a homeomorphic coordinate system for the interior of the observed-law simplex.  Put
\[
\theta_\star=(1/2,4/5,1/5),
\qquad \tau_\star=3/10.
\]
Write \(C_\theta\) and \(\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_\theta\) for the two frontiers at the law indexed by \(\theta\).  The proved theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}strict\mbox{-}jensen\mbox{-}gap}\) gives
\[
C_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star)=\frac9{70},qquad
\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star)=\frac9{91},qquad
g_\star:=\frac9{70}-\frac9{91}=\frac{27}{910}.
\tag{24}
\]

We first prove continuity of the full-law value at \(\theta_\star\).  For a general \(\theta\), define from the frozen scalar program
\[
A_\theta=e(1-p_1),\qquad
B_\theta=(1-e)p_0,\qquad
D_\theta=1-ep_1-(1-e)p_0,
\]
and evaluate \(L_\tau,U_\tau,F_\tau\) at \(\tau=\tau_\star\) and \(\Gamma=4\).  At \(\theta_\star\),
\[
A_{\theta_\star}=B_{\theta_\star}=\frac1{10},qquad
D_{\theta_\star}=\frac12,qquad
\ell=\frac15,qquad u=\frac45.
\]
The three lower-face values are
\[
\frac18,\qquad\frac15,\qquad\frac{13}{50},
\]
and the three upper-face values are
\[
\frac12,\qquad\frac{23}{40},\qquad\frac{11}{25}.
\]
Consequently
\[
[L_{\theta_\star},U_{\theta_\star}]
=[13/50,11/25].
\tag{25}
\]
The point \(v_\star=7/20\) has distance \(9/100\) from both endpoints, and direct substitution gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
F_{\theta_\star}(v_\star)
&=4\left(\frac1{35}+\frac5{28}+\frac3{40}-\frac14\right)\\
&=4\left(\frac9{280}\right)=\frac9{70}
=C_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star).
\end{aligned}
\tag{26}
\]

Each candidate face defining \(L_\theta\) and \(U_\theta\) is continuous at \(\theta_\star\), since \(e\in(0,1)\) and therefore \(0<\ell(e)<u(e)<1\).  A finite maximum or minimum of continuous functions is continuous.  Hence, on some neighborhood of \(\theta_\star\), the point \(v_\star\) remains feasible and all feasible intervals lie in a common compact subinterval on which
\[
v,\quad1-\tau_\star-v,\quad e,\quad1-e
\]
are bounded away from zero.  The formula defining \(F_\theta(v)\) is therefore jointly continuous there.

To prove continuity of the value rather than merely pointwise continuity of its objective, take an arbitrary sequence \(\theta_n\to\theta_\star\).  Feasibility of the fixed interior point \(v_\star\), (26), and the scalar-program equality from \(\mathrm{thm{:}binary\mbox{-}phase\mbox{-}catalog}\) give
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}C_{\theta_n}(\tau_\star)
\leq\lim_{n\to\infty}F_{\theta_n}(v_\star)
=C_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star).
\tag{27}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), let \(v_n\in[L_{\theta_n},U_{\theta_n}]\) be a minimizer, whose existence is also part of that scalar-program characterization.  Along a subsequence realizing the lower limit, compactness gives a further subsequence, not relabeled, with \(v_n\to v\).  Continuity of the two endpoints implies \(v\in[L_{\theta_\star},U_{\theta_\star}]\), and joint continuity gives
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}C_{\theta_n}(\tau_\star)
=F_{\theta_\star}(v)
\geq C_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star).
\tag{28}
\]
Equations (27)--(28) prove continuity of \(C_\theta(\tau_\star)\) at \(\theta_\star\).

We next prove continuity of the box-augmented value.  Put \(r_1=ew(\,\cdot\,,1)\) and \(r_0=(1-e)w(\,\cdot\,,0)\).  When \(\Gamma=4\), direct substitution into the odds faces gives their respective lower and upper endpoints
\[
a_1(e)=\frac{1+3e}{4},\quad b_1(e)=4-3e,
\qquad
a_0(e)=\frac{4-3e}{4},\quad b_0(e)=1+3e.
\tag{29}
\]
For \(z\in\{0,1\}\), use \(p_z=p_1\) for \(z=1\) and \(p_z=p_0\) for \(z=0\), and define
\[
\lambda_z(\theta)
=\max\{a_z(e)p_z,\,1-b_z(e)(1-p_z)\},
\qquad
\nu_z(\theta)
=\min\{b_z(e)p_z,\,1-a_z(e)(1-p_z)\}.
\tag{30}
\]
If \(m_z\) is the normalized reweighted mean in arm \(z\), binary support and normalization force
\[
r_z(1)=m_z/p_z,
\qquad r_z(0)=(1-m_z)/(1-p_z).
\tag{31}
\]
Conversely, (31) defines normalized weights for every \(m_z\in(0,1)\).  Applying both box inequalities from (29) to both values in (31) shows, in both directions, that the attainable means are exactly
\[
m_z\in[\lambda_z(\theta),\nu_z(\theta)].
\tag{32}
\]
With \(x=m_0\) and \(m_1=x+\tau_\star\), the relaxed ATE slice is thus exactly
\[
\widetilde L_\theta
:=\max\{\lambda_0(\theta),\lambda_1(\theta)-\tau_\star\}
\leq x\leq
\min\{\nu_0(\theta),\nu_1(\theta)-\tau_\star\}
=:\widetilde U_\theta.
\tag{33}
\]
The algebra in (14), now multiplied by the observed arm probabilities, makes its objective
\[
\widetilde F_\theta(x)
=e\,g_{p_1}(x+\tau_\star)+(1-e)g_{p_0}(x),
\qquad
g_p(m)=\frac{(m-p)^2}{m(1-m)}.
\tag{34}
\]
At \(\theta_\star\), equations (29)--(33) give
\[
[\widetilde L_{\theta_\star},\widetilde U_{\theta_\star}]
=[1/5,1/2].
\tag{35}
\]
The minimizer \(x_\star=7/20\) from \(\mathrm{thm{:}strict\mbox{-}jensen\mbox{-}gap}\) is at distance \(3/20\) from both endpoints and satisfies
\[
\widetilde F_{\theta_\star}(x_\star)
=\frac9{91}
=\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star).
\tag{36}
\]
All endpoints in (33) are continuous by (29)--(30).  Near (35), the quantities
\[
x,\quad1-x,\quad x+\tau_\star,\quad1-x-\tau_\star
\]
are uniformly positive, so (34) is jointly continuous on a common compact interval.  Repeating the sequence proof in (27)--(28), with the strictly feasible point \(x_\star\) for the upper limit and minimizers in the compact intervals (33) for the lower limit, proves
\[
\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_\theta(\tau_\star)
\longrightarrow
\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_{\theta_\star}(\tau_\star)
\quad\text{as }\theta\to\theta_\star.
\tag{37}
\]

By (24), (27)--(28), and (37), there is \(\eta_0>0\) such that the strict cube
\[
B_{\eta_0}:=
\{\theta:\|\theta-\theta_\star\|_\infty<\eta_0\}
\]
keeps both scalar intervals nonempty and satisfies
\[
\left|C_\theta(\tau_\star)-\frac9{70}\right|<\frac{g_\star}{4},
\qquad
\left|\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_\theta(\tau_\star)-\frac9{91}\right|<\frac{g_\star}{4}.
\tag{38}
\]
Choose
\[
0<\eta\leq\min\{\eta_0,1/10\}.
\tag{39}
\]
For every \(\theta\in B_\eta\),
\[
 e\geq\frac12-\eta,quad 1-e\geq\frac12-\eta,quad
p_1\geq\frac45-\eta,quad1-p_1\geq\frac15-\eta,quad
p_0\geq\frac15-\eta,quad1-p_0\geq\frac45-\eta.
\tag{40}
\]
It follows from (22) and (40) that every one of the four observable cells has the explicit positive lower bound
\[
P(Z=z,Y=y)
\geq\left(\frac12-\eta\right)
       \left(\frac15-\eta\right)>0.
\tag{41}
\]
Likewise, both conditional arm variances and the treatment variance obey
\[
p_z(1-p_z)
\geq\left(\frac15-\eta\right)
       \left(\frac45-\eta\right)>0
\quad(z=0,1),
\qquad
e(1-e)\geq\left(\frac12-\eta\right)^2>0.
\tag{42}
\]
Thus the neighborhood is uniformly separated from every observable support boundary relevant to the two programs.

The parameter cube \(B_\eta\) is nonempty and has three-dimensional Lebesgue volume \((2\eta)^3>0\).  Moreover, in the first three observable-cell coordinates in (22), the Jacobian determinant of the parameter-to-law map has absolute value
\[
e(1-e)\geq\left(\frac12-\eta\right)^2>0.
\tag{43}
\]
The explicit continuous inverse (23) therefore shows directly that its image is a nonempty open Euclidean neighborhood in the interior of the observed-law simplex.  It contains an ordinary Euclidean ball and hence has positive three-dimensional Lebesgue volume; in particular, the neighborhood is not a lower-dimensional path or face.  This records both positive parameter volume and positive observable support.

Finally, subtracting the two inequalities in (38) and using (24) gives, throughout \(B_\eta\),
\[
C_\theta(3/10)-\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_\theta(3/10)
\geq g_\star-\frac{g_\star}{2}
=\frac{27}{1820}>0.
\tag{44}
\]
The preserved strict interior points \(v_\star\) and \(x_\star\) prove finiteness of both frontier values there.  Equations (39)--(44) supply the requested uniformly supported, positive-volume open neighborhood and complete the proof.
